summary: A toggle for a single on/off setting that takes effect as a form value: it submits its value while on, resets with its form, follows a disabled fieldset and validates required. Carries a label, an optional description and an error message, in two sizes.

checked.note: Whether the switch is on. The attribute is the default (initial and reset) state, like a native checkbox; the property is the live state and is not reflected, so a form reset can return to the attribute. Registered alias of the canonical selected (spec/api.json aliases.checked): the native and reference name every form author expects.

name.note: The name the value is submitted under. Without a name the switch submits nothing.

value.note: What is submitted under name while the switch is on. Nothing is submitted while it is off (native checkbox rule).

label.note: Visible text beside the switch and its accessible name. A switch without a label warns once at runtime.

description.note: Optional hint under the label, announced as the switch's description.

errorMessage.note: Why the setting is not accepted. Shown, and announced as part of the description, only while validation is error.

validation.note: error shows the error look and errorMessage and marks the switch invalid for assistive technology. It does not block form submission by itself; required does that (PROPOSAL, see openQuestions Q2).

size.note: Track and thumb size. Canonical vocabulary names for the reference's sm and default (PROPOSAL, Q3).

disabled.note: Cannot be focused, toggled or submitted. A disabled fieldset ancestor has the same effect without changing this attribute.

required.note: The switch must be on for its form to be valid (valueMissing while off), like a required native checkbox.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: Lays out the control row and the text below it. The whole row, label included, toggles on press.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: The focusable element exposed with the switch role. Holds the track and thumb; it owns the checked state, the name, the description and the validity.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: Pill-shaped bar; filled with the primary color while on and the input color while off.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Circle that sits at the start while off and slides to the end while on (mirrored in right-to-left).

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Visible label beside the track, at the end in reading order; it names the switch.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Error text under the label (after the description), shown only while validation is error and errorMessage is not empty.

change.note: Fires on the host after the user toggles the switch (pointer, label or Space), once checked and the form value are updated. Never fires for a programmatic change of checked or for a form reset.

input.note: Fires with every user toggle, just before change, as on a native checkbox.

hover.note: No visual change, as in the reference; the pointer cursor signals the row is pressable.

focus-visible.note: A ring around the track; not shown for pointer focus.

checked.note: Track fills with primary; thumb moves to the end.

disabled.trigger: disabled is true, or a disabled fieldset ancestor.
disabled.note: Whole row dimmed, not focusable, not pressable, not submitted.

invalid.note: Track outlined in destructive; errorMessage shown under the label and added to the description.

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: label prop (rendered as the visible label, associated with the control). An external label pointing at the switch activates it but does not name it, so label stays required.

formAssociation.note: Form-associated from the first implementation (rule form-associated-controls). Submits value under name while on, nothing while off; form reset restores the checked attribute; a disabled fieldset disables it without touching its disabled attribute; required makes an off switch valueMissing, with the browser's validation message, and reportValidity focuses it; saved form state is restored on navigation back; an external label activates it.

accessibility.targetSize: The pressable area is the whole row, label included, so it meets 24 by 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8) even for the small track (24 by 16).
accessibility.focusRingVisible: Ring of focus.ring.width in color.ring around the track on keyboard focus only.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Warns once at runtime when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to and from the switch (one tab stop). A disabled switch is skipped.
keyboard.Space: Toggles the switch and fires input then change.
keyboard.Enter: Does not toggle; submits the owning form, like a native checkbox (PROPOSAL, Q1).

aria: role=switch on the control, with aria-checked derived from the checked state (true or false, never mixed).
aria-describedby lists the description and, while validation is error, the error message.
required is exposed as required (aria-required) on the control.
disabled is exposed as disabled on the control.
announcements: On focus: label, switch, on/off state, then description and error message.
On toggle: the new state (on or off).

useCases.when: A single setting that is either on or off and takes effect as soon as it is toggled (notifications, dark mode, airplane mode).
useCases.use: Switch with a label naming the setting, not the action.

useCases.when: The setting needs a sentence of context or a consequence.
The setting is part of a form that is submitted (a preferences form).
useCases.use: Switch with name (and value when the server expects something other than on).

useCases.when: The form cannot be sent until the person turns the setting on (accepting terms).
useCases.use: Switch with required; prefer a Checkbox when this is an agreement rather than a setting.

useCases.when: Server or cross-field validation rejected the setting.
useCases.use: validation error with an errorMessage that says how to fix it.

useCases.when: Dense layouts (table rows, compact settings lists).

antiPatterns.pattern: Using a switch for a choice that only applies after a Submit or Save press, or for selecting items in a list.
antiPatterns.why: A switch reads as an immediate on/off setting (WAI-ARIA APG switch pattern); people expect the change to take effect at once.
antiPatterns.alternative: Checkbox for agreements, options confirmed on submit, and multi-select.

antiPatterns.pattern: A label that changes with the state ("On"/"Off" or "Enable"/"Disable").
antiPatterns.why: The APG switch pattern: the label stays the same when the state changes; the state is announced separately, so a changing label is announced twice or contradicts it.
antiPatterns.alternative: A fixed label naming the setting ("Notifications").

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch without a visible or accessible label.
antiPatterns.why: Role, state and value are announced with no name (WCAG 4.1.2), and sighted people cannot tell what it controls.
A switch is only on or off; the APG switch has no mixed state.
antiPatterns.alternative: Checkbox, which has an indeterminate state.

drift.realization: The visual reference names them sm | default; this system uses the canonical size vocabulary.
The visual reference uses 32 by about 18.4 and 24 by 14; the system's size scale rounds them to whole steps.
The visual reference uses the ring color at 50% alpha; there is no alpha token, and full strength meets 3:1 non-text contrast.

drift.contract: Track border in color.destructive plus visible error text
drift.realization: The visual reference adds a destructive ring at 20% alpha and has no error text inside the component.

drift.contract: label, description and errorMessage are props of the switch
drift.realization: The visual reference composes a separate Label and Field around the switch; here they are built in so the accessible name and description cannot be forgotten.

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes. Drafted from the visual reference set in the project configuration (UI, API, visuals), the WAI-ARIA APG switch pattern (keyboard, ARIA) and the form-associated-controls rule.

openQuestions.question: Should Enter toggle the switch (the APG lists Enter as optional) or submit the form?
openQuestions.recommendation: Enter submits the owning form and does not toggle, like a native checkbox; Space toggles.
openQuestions.answer: Recommendation taken: Space toggles; Enter submits the form (implicit submission). Unattended session, no reviewer available.

openQuestions.question: Should validation error also make the switch invalid for constraint validation (block submit), or only show the error look?
openQuestions.recommendation: Only the look and aria-invalid; native validity comes from required alone, so a server-side error never silently blocks a resubmit.
openQuestions.answer: Recommendation taken: validation is presentational plus aria-invalid; required drives valueMissing. Unattended session, no reviewer available.

openQuestions.question: Name the sizes after the reference (sm, default) through an alias, or use the canonical size vocabulary?
openQuestions.recommendation: Canonical small and medium: no alias divergence to migrate later; the reference names are recorded as drift.
openQuestions.answer: Recommendation taken: small | medium, default medium. Unattended session, no reviewer available.

openQuestions.question: Does form reset return to the checked attribute (native default state) or to the state at first render?
openQuestions.recommendation: The checked attribute, like a native checkbox's defaultChecked; the checked property is the live state and is not reflected.
openQuestions.answer: Recommendation taken. Unattended session, no reviewer available.

openQuestions.question: Where does the label sit, and is it built in or composed from a separate Label component?
openQuestions.recommendation: Built in, after the track in reading order (the common settings-row layout); no separate Label dependency.
openQuestions.answer: Recommendation taken. Unattended session, no reviewer available.

openQuestions.question: Manual screen-reader pass (VoiceOver with Safari, NVDA with Firefox or Chrome) of name, role, on/off state, description and error announcements.
openQuestions.recommendation: Run it before the component moves to stable.
